scope: Replace the selected nested list with one native sourced mythology network, inspired by TinyCharts #spread.
cause: The old nested structure only connected Apollo to Zeus; Leto appeared as a label. A root-reachability test could not detect lost co-parents.
facts: Each individual has one canonical ID. Lineages retain source-specific parent sets. Emergence, creation, story ties, membership and game continuity remain distinct. Every endpoint and reference resolves. No fabricated universal ancestor.

failing_lines: Both named parents need real node connections, not a coparent label

Desktop Chrome responsive view tested; physical touch hardware not run.
The complete downloadable JSON includes game spoilers.
privacy: Journal body and media publication states unchanged. The authored entry remains a private draft; only the general mythology catalogue and native component are committed.

calibration.claim: A normalized source-specific graph restores both-parent connections lost by the nested list
The native network has no internal scroll area or horizontal overflow at 320px and 390px
Wrapped inline reveal text left a center click gap; a contiguous gray cover fixes the mobile click
Source selection reorders the complete network and changes emphasized Melinoe parentage while retaining hidden reveals

comparison.behavior: Changing a telling reorders all 433 nodes, emphasizes selected source relationships, and preserves other accounts as pale context. An individual origin radio overrides only that figure; new telling or figure clears the override.
comparison.browser: Verified Melinoe changes from Hades/Persephone to Zeus/Persephone, with different coordinates and 952 spoiler-safe connections. Per-origin Hades override within Orphic view passed; telling change clears it. 320px and 390px remain free of horizontal overflow and internal scrollbars.
comparison.review: One independent code/source review for this follow-up; no findings at or above threshold.
comparison.notes: These are reading groups, not reconciled single-source family trees. Homeric hymns are not assigned to one author; Orphic traditions remain plural.
